doc.title: Bill Berry and Buster Cooper interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Opening and Berry's start on trumpet
summary: Woods introduces the Statesmen of Jazz; Berry got a trumpet for Christmas, with a good teacher and musician parents.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: We are filming interviews with America’s greatest jazz men for the Hamilton College Jazz Archives. And we are blessed today to have two fabulous musicians from a newly formed group called the Statesmen of Jazz. Bill Berry and Buster Cooper. Pleased to have you gentlemen. Tell us how you got started playing the trumpet.

Well let’s see — how I got started. Well I always wanted to play. Actually I wanted to play trombone but Buster got that. But I pestered my folks until they bought me a horn for Christmas one year, and I’ve been playing the thing ever since.
How was the music in the school systems? Did that help?
I had a very good music teacher in high school but my parents were also musicians.
